items.text: Yousef Miri was killed on the evening of Esfand 26, 1404, on Hafez Street in Isfahan by gunfire from Basij forces. This incident occurred on Chaharshanbe Suri night. His name remains as a reminder for freedom seekers.
A video shows a protester in Talesh writing the slogan "Long live the king" on a wall. The video was received by Iran International. This event took place in Talesh.

Ahmad Alamolhoda stated that the leadership can no longer directly communicate with the people, creating a gap that the intellectual current seeks to exploit to remove the leadership. He emphasized their duty to bring people closer to the leadership and fill this gap. Alamolhoda added that if the leadership is not harmed, the clergy will remain in power.

A video shows a protester in Bastak city, Hormozgan province, writing the slogans "Long live the Shah" and "Death to the regime" on a wall. The video was received by Iran International. This incident was reported in Bastak.

Fatemeh Mohajerani, the government spokesperson, refrained from announcing statistics on severe poverty in Iran. She stated that publishing these figures requires permission from the Supreme National Security Council. Security considerations were cited as the reason for this restriction.

Bloomberg reported that Turkey faces the risk of losing a key energy supply source if Washington's threat to economically isolate Tehran is carried out. This situation could create new challenges for Turkey's energy security and economy. The report was provided by Narges Horkhsh from Iran International.

Two impeachment motions against the Minister of Sports and Youth have been registered in parliament due to administrative corruption, weak international performance, and election engineering in federations. A complaint has also been filed regarding the violation of the former bodybuilding federation president's rights and the minister's disregard for postponing elections. The minister is scheduled to appear before the Article 90 commission for questioning within two weeks.

Morteza Kazemian referred to Kayhan newspaper's criticism of the Pakistani Prime Minister's trip to Tehran and the Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister's remarks about the insecurity in the Strait of Hormuz. He said the demands of Tehran and Washington make an agreement difficult. Kazemian highlighted Tehran's hard stance and the continuation of tensions with the US.

John Ratcliffe, the CIA director, has traveled to Russia. This trip occurred amid serious tensions between the US and Russia. It is likely that topics such as the Ukraine war, Middle East developments, and the Islamic Republic dossier were discussed.

A 19-year-old resident of Karaj was shot with a live bullet while helping an injured protester during the December 2025 protests and suffered severe injury to his left knee. After about a month and a half of treatment and several surgeries, part of his leg was amputated. He is now facing financial difficulties to cover treatment and prosthetic costs.
A citizen on September 4 mentioned a sharp increase in food prices. He said sanctions and economic war pressures have affected people's lives. The living conditions have become more difficult.

The Mes Shahr-e Babak club has officially filed a complaint about Yaser Asani's participation in three recent Esteghlal matches to the disciplinary committee of the Football Federation. The league organization stated that Asani's contract with Esteghlal is valid for another season and no official termination has been registered. Esteghlal's main concern is the potential complaints from rivals in the Asian Elite League.

Abbas Shiri stated that over 46 to 48 percent of work-related accidents occur in the construction industry. He pointed to weak safety training and oversight by the Ministry of Labor and described the safety conditions at construction sites as dire. He also mentioned the death of two workers in Qom and the lack of insurance for many workers.

Citizens from various provinces in Iran have reported that fuel shortages have led to long queues for gasoline. Gas stations in Babol are operating with generators due to power outages, and people are waiting until midnight. Long lines have also been observed in Mashhad and the Karaj highway for fuel.

Amirhossein Bedaqi, an electrical engineering student at Tabriz University, has been held in Urmia prison for over four months without a judicial decision. His detention status remains unresolved. This issue was reported by Harana News Agency.

Morad Veysi, a senior analyst at Iran International, highlighted concerns of families about school safety and students' academic decline. There is also a reported shortage of gasoline and diesel and closure of some fuel stations in Tehran. Some truck drivers wait in line for one to two days to get fuel.

Morad Veysi, a senior analyst at Iran International, said that any international development weakening the Islamic Republic benefits the people. The people welcome increased pressure and Trump's refusal to reach an agreement with the Islamic Republic. They want this campaign to have a practical impact on accelerating the overthrow of the Islamic Republic.

Morad Veisi said that the people of Iran welcome Trump's call to stop the killing of protesters. They expect the US government to show this stance through concrete actions against those running the repression machinery. Many on social media also call for Israel to be allowed to target government centers and officials involved in the killings.

The family of Lindsay and Craig Foreman, who have been imprisoned in Iran for 600 days, has requested an urgent meeting with British officials. They expressed concern about the couple's health following a prolonged hunger strike. British embassy staff have returned to Iran, but a meeting has not been confirmed.
The disciplinary committee of Shiraz University has summoned about 20 students and opened disciplinary cases against them.

Sadegh Hosseini, an economic expert, emphasized the necessity of economic reforms in Iran. He warned that if Iran reaches a situation similar to Venezuela, worse events will occur. He also called for gasoline price reforms.

The Israeli Prime Minister said he discussed three options with Trump regarding the Islamic Republic: reaching an agreement, military action, or intensifying the blockade. He believes reaching an agreement with the current Iranian government is impossible and Israel is prepared for a severe defense if attacked. Trump has also increased pressure on those aiding the Iranian government.

Alireza Dabir, head of the Wrestling Federation, stated that due to visa issues, the Iranian national wrestling team might not be sent to the World Junior Championships in the USA. He said if the US denies a visa to any team member, the team will not be sent.

Newsmax reported that Yair Netanyahu was targeted in an assassination plot in Miami. Israeli intelligence identified an Iranian group monitoring his residence and daily routine. After the threat was discovered, Yair Netanyahu and his guards were ordered to leave Miami immediately.

Parents complain about the soaring school expenses. Students have also expressed concerns about increased dormitory fees and financial pressures. Reports of educational space shortages in some cities have been received.

Ali Hossein Ghazizadeh said that the US naval blockade and sanctions could inflict irreparable damage on the Islamic Republic. He added that reduced military capability and limited oil sales have weakened the regime's conditions. He also mentioned that sanctions might facilitate the US goals in the nuclear and missile file.
Two rangers in the protected area of Mand in Bushehr province were injured during their mission due to shooting by illegal hunters using a pellet gun.

The Football Federation board extended Amir Ghalenoei's contract as the national team coach until the end of the 2027 Asian Championship. Ghalenoei presented his plan for the national team. The Asian Championship will be held in Saudi Arabia in January and February of this year.

Videos sent by citizens to Iran International show long queues forming to receive diesel and gasoline in the Tehranpars and Dadman neighborhoods in Tehran. People are standing in line for fuel in these areas. This situation has been reported in the city of Tehran.

Mohammad Akraminia, the army spokesperson, stated that despite follow-ups, Qatari officials are unaware of the status of three missing army pilots in Qatar. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the presidential office, and the army have pursued the pilots' status through the Qatari government and army. So far, no response has been received from Qatari officials.

The World Water Week is being held in Stockholm, Sweden, focusing on climate challenges, drought, and equitable access to water. Kaveh Madani, an Iranian researcher, will receive the 2026 award. This international event highlights important water issues.

Romina Pourmokhtari, Sweden's Minister of Climate and Environment, accused the Islamic Republic of crimes, killings, and human rights violations. She stated that Sweden is not willing to cooperate directly with Tehran on environmental issues and climate crisis mitigation. These remarks were made in an interview with an Iran International journalist.

ISNA news agency reported that Hadi Choopan has missed the 2026 Mr. Olympia competition due to visa issues. Choopan intended to visit the US embassy in the UAE for a visa interview, but was unable to do so because the UAE denied him entry.
A citizen in Isfahan needs to visit a clinic after back surgery. Due to a power outage, using the clinic's elevator is impossible. This issue was reported in a video to Iran International.

New details about Majid Adineh's life have been released. He was an activist arrested on January 9 and executed on August 23 by the Revolutionary Court of Karaj. For over two decades, he supported orphaned children and homeless individuals, dedicating much of his assets and income to charity work.

Masoud Pezeshkian stated that people have shown they will fight if necessary, but war is not always the solution. He called the recent agreement a document of pride for the Islamic Republic and emphasized that peace should not be abandoned. He also noted that all members of the National Security Council except one supported the agreement.

The Football Federation's board approved Amir Ghalenoei's continuation as head coach of Iran's national football team until the end of the 2027 Asian Cup. This decision was made after reviewing the team's performance and future plans. Mozdak Mirzaei also evaluated the contract extension.

The family of Lindsey and Craig Foreman, British prisoners in Iran, criticized the UK government for not taking action to meet them. Despite the reopening of the London embassy in Tehran, no meeting has taken place. Joe Bennet stated that the couple has not received proper medical examinations after a hunger strike.

Three Indian refineries and an international energy company have decided not to use 45 Iranian blacklisted ships. The Financial Times reported the stopping of 13 Iranian oil tankers near Sri Lankan waters. These actions follow threats by the Islamic Republic against countries participating in the US economic isolation campaign.

Citizens reported that power was cut off at night in Sanandaj without prior notice. Additionally, a beach soccer Premier League match in Rudsar was stopped due to a power outage. These events were reported by Iran International.

Hossein Mohibi, spokesperson for the IRGC, stated that the Strait of Hormuz will not be opened unless the US accepts Iran's conditions. He mentioned negotiations with Oman regarding the share of the two countries in the waters of the strait and said US interference delayed the implementation of agreements. He also emphasized that the Strait of Hormuz and the nearby waterway near Oman are under Iran's control.

Seyed Ahmad Seyed Abdollahi, a political prisoner, was granted a five-day leave from Borujen prison on Tuesday, 3 Shahrivar 1405. The indictment for his case, accusing him of propaganda against the Islamic Republic, was issued and sent to the Borujen Revolutionary Court. Evidence extracted from his mobile phone was cited as part of the charges.

Snap drivers in Tehran face reduced fuel quotas and a sharp increase in fares. Motorcycle fuel quotas have decreased from 25 to 15 liters, and gas stations are either closed or crowded. Additionally, GPS systems have been disrupted since Saturday, making work difficult for drivers.

The withdrawal from Iran's strategic fuel reserves has reached a red alert stage and may be depleted within weeks. This issue has caused a dispute between Masoud Pezeshkian's government and the Revolutionary Guards. The Guards oppose unlimited withdrawal, but the government wants to continue withdrawing.

Mohammad Ebrahimi, arrested during the January 2026 protests, was sentenced to 15 years in prison by the appeals court. He was arrested in early February 2026 in Tehran. His previous 20-year sentence was reduced after the appeal.

Ahmad Keyshams, a citizen from Izeh, has been held in Sheiban prison in Ahvaz for over 9 months with an unclear judicial status. He suffers from kidney disease and vision problems but has been deprived of proper medical care. No court session has been held to address his charges so far.
A citizen told Iran International in a video that the price of several food items has reached about five million tomans. This occurred on the eve of the fifth decade of the Islamic Republic's rule.

Fatemeh Mohajerani said a citizen told her "may you die" because of her support for Mohammad Javad Zarif. Mohajerani called Zarif a soldier of the system and did not consider Hamid Rasaei a soldier of the system. She referred to Rasaei's statement suggesting targeting Donald Trump with a missile.
A man was killed in the Sidi neighborhood of Mashhad with an honor motive. The suspect was arrested after five months. The case has been sent to court.

Donald Trump said in an interview that he does not think Mojtaba Khamenei has been killed and that he was severely injured. Trump added that even if Mojtaba Khamenei is dead, the Islamic Republic is putting on a good show. He also said that reaching an agreement with the Islamic Republic is not easy and they are not very committed to principles.

Masih Shahverdi, a former youth team player for Sepahan club, was shot and killed by government forces during protests on January 8, 2026, in the "Khane Isfahan" area. He was 19 years old and had only two months left of his military service. Masih Shahverdi died around 1 AM in his brother's arms.

Benjamin Netanyahu expressed doubt about the possibility of the US reaching a diplomatic agreement with Iran. He said Israel does not oppose a good agreement but believes it is impossible to reach an agreement with the rulers of Iran. Netanyahu called the Iranian rulers "savages" and said no agreement can be reached with them.

Masoud Pezeshkian reiterated the necessity of ending the war with the United States, stating that war is not always the solution. He called Iran the victor and added that the path can be passed with prudence and thought. These remarks were made at a public ceremony.

A report by Ruydad24 indicates that installment purchases in Iran have expanded from expensive goods to everyday and supermarket items. This trend is due to increasing poverty and reduced purchasing power. People are using future income to meet current needs and are transferring economic pressure to future months.
A citizen in a video to Iran International said that the economic war has affected drug prices. He also stated that the government must go and the people of Iran will be victorious.

Abolfazl Shekarchi called Persian-language media outside the country enemies, including Iran International, BBC, and Radio Farda. He stated that these media and their activists can be placed in the military target bank. He also emphasized that these media are not considered media by the armed forces.

Marco Rubio stated that the United States does not intend to start a new round of military attacks against the Islamic Republic. Benjamin Netanyahu described Iranian officials as "brutal" and said the challenge is not over yet. He emphasized that Israel must bring this challenge to an end.
Arman Rahimabadi has been sentenced to five years in prison. He was arrested in January 2026 in Birjand and requires treatment outside prison. His sentence was confirmed by the appeals court.

Masoud Pezeshkian stated at the inauguration ceremony of development projects that the country is in the worst economic war situation. He emphasized that economic pressures may not be as visible as the missile war, but work continues. Pezeshkian expressed hope that with people's unity and officials' responsibility, problems will be quickly resolved and the country will prosper.

Floods and landslides in Nepal near the Tibet border have caused at least 95 deaths. 403 people are still missing, including 61 Nepalis and 341 foreigners. Rescue and search operations continue in the border areas between Nepal and China.

Joseph Aoun, the President of Lebanon, stated that Beirut seeks the liberation of southern Lebanon, the return of prisoners, and the deployment of the army at the country's borders. Mi Farhat, a reporter from Iran International, reported from a checkpoint in Nabatieh in southern Lebanon.
A citizen sent a video to Iran International stating that they paid 4,800,000 tomans for fruits, vegetables, and one kilogram of chicken meat, expressing concern about the current situation.

Donald Trump stated that there is no specific timeline for resuming negotiations with the Islamic Republic and he is not in a hurry. He said that both military attacks and economic pressure by the US against the Islamic Republic are effective. Trump also added that Iran's economy is collapsing.

Iran International reported that the Iranian government is seeking to revive the Special Operations Department in the Ministry of Intelligence. The stated goal is to avenge Khamenei and assassinate leaders of the US and Israel. This information was released alongside new details about a plot to assassinate Netanyahu's son.

Neda Badakhsh, a 62-year-old Bahá'í citizen imprisoned in Dolatabad Prison in Isfahan, has been deprived of specialized medical care despite suffering from multiple illnesses including diabetes and sciatica. A specialist doctor has recommended that she undergo examination and specialized treatment every three months. Her medical leave requests have not been approved, and she has not been transferred to medical centers outside the prison.

The Stockholm World Water Week is being held focusing on water crisis, climate change, and water governance. The prestigious Stockholm Water Prize is awarded to Kaveh Madani for his work in water resource management and policy. This news was reported by Mehran Abbassian.

UEFA intends to withdraw its threat to boycott FIFA competitions after receiving guarantees that the plan to sell World Cup shares will not be repeated. Previously, 55 European countries had agreed to boycott these competitions. However, UEFA plans to intensify actions against Gianni Infantino due to this plan.

The Minister of Communications stated that the filtering issue must be closed in the country. He warned that the use of VPNs causes significant damage and reduces internet quality. He also emphasized that governance in cyberspace cannot be achieved solely through technical means and that people will become dissatisfied.

A citizen reported that on the 4th of Shahrivar in Tehran, a long line of cars formed in front of the Pasdaran gas station. The line extended to Pasdaran intersection. This report was sent to Iran International.

Nikolay Mladenov, the representative of the Gaza peace delegation, stated that Hamas has accepted the disarmament plan. Hamas demands Israel to adhere to its commitments in Donald Trump's 20-point peace plan. Mladenov said Israel must reaffirm its commitments under this plan.

The head of the Atomic Energy Organization stated that until inspection protocols for sites attacked militarily are established, the IAEA cannot claim inspections. He emphasized that the agency must clarify its stance on site security. He also mentioned that the US and Israel are pressuring the agency to inspect the damaged sites.

Videos sent to Iran International show that the historic Municipality Square in Rasht has been occupied with government banners. These videos are from Wednesday, the 4th of Shahrivar. This issue was reported by Iran International.

The spokesperson of the Revolutionary Guards stated that Iran and Oman have reached preliminary agreements on their share of the waters and revenues of the Strait of Hormuz after one month of negotiations. He said the Strait of Hormuz and the waterway near Oman are now under the control of the Islamic Republic. The United States was also accused of obstructing the negotiation process.

Security forces prevented the anniversary ceremony of Aref Mirmousavi in his hometown, Dehshal. His family was given a written commitment not to attend the ceremony. Several family members were injured during the prevention of people's attendance.

The management of the Amur gas chemical complex in Russia announced that seven people were killed and 152 injured in the fire on Tuesday. Thirty-six of the injured were hospitalized. Earlier, it was reported that six Chinese citizens were killed and nine others were missing.
A video shows that fuel station 263 Ghadir on Kharazi Highway in Tehran was closed on Wednesday, 4th of Shahrivar, due to lack of gasoline.

The German Finance Minister stated that the Iran war has caused disruptions in the bond market. The German Interior Minister also warned about foreign threats. This report was prepared by Ahmad Samadi from Iran International.

On Tuesday, 24 August, the home of Keyhan and Fereshteh Atefi, a Baha'i couple in Isfahan, was searched by intelligence officers. During the search, several personal belongings, a car, and assets of the couple were confiscated. The confiscated items included a television, vacuum cleaner, toolbox, car, gold, valuable objects, communication devices, and the grandchild's toys.

A tornado formed on Monday, August 24, in southern Carcassonne, France. The tornado reached the Puma area around 5 PM, injuring at least 26 people and causing power outages for about 2800 households. The French meteorological organization had previously issued a thunderstorm warning.

Abbas Araghchi wrote a letter to the UN Secretary-General and Security Council describing the US economic expulsion operations against Iran as illegal. He called for condemnation of this action and an immediate halt to US threats. Araghchi urged the UN to compel the US to stop its aggressive measures.

Ahmad Donyamali, the Minister of Sports, reached an agreement with football federation officials and the clubs Esteghlal and Tractor for the participation of their players in the Asian Games in Nagoya. Previously, there were concerns about the scheduling conflict between the Premier League and Elite League matches. Plans will be coordinated to meet the needs of the national under-23 team and the two Iranian representatives in the Elite League.

The Kremlin has confirmed the CIA chief's trip to Moscow. The reason for the trip was communication between intelligence services. It was reported that messages regarding the Strait of Hormuz and sanctions were conveyed.

Iran and Oman have reached an agreement to close the southern route of the Strait of Hormuz. Two proposed routes by the Islamic Republic will be announced to the International Maritime Organization. The status of mines in the strait remains unclear, and the US claims to have cleared mines from the main route of Hormuz.

Sudden floods in the Nepal-China border area caused at least 98 deaths and hundreds of missing people. Nepal's Prime Minister's office reported 95 deaths. China's CCTV network reported a landslide in Tibet with three deaths and 265 missing.

Snap drivers face challenges such as rising fuel costs, vehicle repairs, and company commissions. Fare prices have increased on various routes, and people in different cities are struggling with power outages and economic difficulties. Some individuals have turned to buying motorcycles due to tough economic conditions, making daily life harder.

Trump has unprecedented doubts about Mojtaba Khamenei's health. He said if Mojtaba Khamenei is dead, it would be well covered up. These statements were made in the audio version of Titraaval with Niousha Saremi.

Rouhollah Rahimpour said Trump's statements about Mojtaba Khamenei's condition reflect the ambiguity created by the Islamic Republic over the past five months. This ambiguity has political and security functions in negotiations and internal and external crises. No definitive information about Mojtaba Khamenei's physical condition or presence has been released.

Donald Trump said he does not think Mojtaba Khamenei is dead, but if he is, the Islamic Republic has hidden it well. He added that Iranian officials always say they need time to consult with him during negotiations. Benjamin Netanyahu called the Iranian rulers "savages" and said reaching an agreement with them is impossible.

Images and reports indicate long queues at fuel stations in various Iranian cities. Taxi fares have increased several times due to fuel shortages and GPS system disruptions. Drivers report the end of fuel quotas and restrictions on purchasing free-market fuel.

The executive deputy of Masoud Pezeshkian stated that gasoline production in Iran is insufficient and the US naval blockade prevents gasoline imports. He also pointed out the unfair distribution of gasoline and called for its reform. The former head of the US Treasury's sanctions targeting office said gasoline imports are the most vulnerable part of Iran's economy under the naval blockade.

A video sent to Iran International shows a long line of vehicles in Tehranpars, Tehran, waiting to receive gasoline and diesel. The video is from Wednesday, the 4th of Shahrivar. People are waiting in line for fuel in this area.

Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, Qatar's Prime Minister and Foreign Minister, will visit Tehran on Thursday, 5th of Shahrivar. The visit aims to discuss ways to reduce tensions and create suitable conditions for dialogue. Freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz will also be addressed during the talks.
Some retirees of Social Security and oil industry workers have expressed dissatisfaction with delays in payment of their salaries and wage arrears. They have requested attention to their situation.

People in various Iranian cities face long gasoline lines and severe economic problems. Education and living costs have risen sharply, causing public concern about the future. Some banks delay returning unauthorized withdrawals.

Madineh Shahnavazi, a Sunni prisoner, has been held in Kerman prison for over 28 months without a clear case status. She was arrested in spring 1403 (2024) and her case is still under investigation in the prosecutor's office. No hearing has been held for her case yet.

Ata Hosseinian said that instead of raising prices, the Islamic Republic is seeking to ration gasoline. Gasoline and diesel reserves are nearing a critical stage, and the government will be forced to limit consumption. Continued maritime blockade could worsen the fuel crisis and cause power plant shutdowns and severe air pollution.

Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf defended dialogue with the United States. Masoud Pezeshkian referred to foreign interference and said the enemy wants to create discord among Islamic Republic officials. Donald Trump did not provide a specific timeline for resuming talks and is not in a hurry to restart negotiations.

An anti-Iranian statement by a broadcaster about sacrificing southern Iran for southern Lebanon sparked a campaign on social media. Young people from the 80s and 90s generations responded with a song by the Sandy group and images of Reza Shah's armbands. Aryan Risbaf reported on this issue.

Abolfazl Shekarchi, senior spokesperson of Iran's armed forces, placed employees of Iran International, BBC Persian, and Radio Farda in a 'military target bank.' He called these employees 'soldiers of Israel and America.' This threat follows ongoing pressure by the Islamic Republic against journalists abroad.

Bloomberg, citing three informed individuals, reported that the US Department of Justice is creating a court to facilitate the military seizure of Iranian oil tankers and taking them as prize. Aaron Reitz, the US Attorney for the Southern District of Texas, confirmed that the DOJ is reviving 'prize courts' and his office is cooperating. According to Bloomberg, this court could provide the necessary legal framework for handling tankers seized by the US in military operations.
Real Madrid defeated Real Sociedad 4-1 in the postponed first week match of La Liga. Kylian Mbappe scored a hat-trick and Vinicius Junior scored one goal. Jude Bellingham provided two assists.

Abolfazl Shekarchi, the spokesperson for the armed forces, called journalists and staff of Iran International, BBC, Manoto, and Radio Farda "Zionist soldiers" and "soldiers of criminal America." He described these networks as hostile and warmongering and said the armed forces consider them in their military target bank. He also claimed these networks are directly connected to Mossad and the CIA and receive guidance from them.

According to Nepal police, at least 160 people died in a sudden flood on Wednesday in the Nepal-China border area. More than 400 tourists, workers, and other citizens are missing. In Mailong, some people escaped the flood path moments before it arrived.

Morad Veysi stated that the severe gasoline shortage in Tehran and other provinces is causing more gas stations to close daily. He described this crisis as a time bomb under the Islamic Republic. He also said that the government has lost the ability to control these crises.

Masoud Pezeshkian referred to foreign interference and said the enemy wants to create discord among Islamic Republic officials. He added that the enemy's goal is to engage them in character assassination against each other.

Morad Veysi, senior analyst at Iran International, said that the combination of increasing crises and the Islamic Republic's inability to control them has put society in a state of pre-uprising. He warned that the risk of the situation going out of government control and the collapse of the regime has increased.
Qalibaf stated that talking with Washington is not taboo amid tensions at the highest levels of government over negotiations with the US. He defended negotiating with the United States.

Alireza Zakani, the mayor of Tehran, announced the construction of three stadiums with capacities between 40,000 and 60,000 in Tehran. He also requested that the renovation of the Azadi Stadium be assigned to the municipality. The Minister of Sports stated that building large stadiums is not currently a government priority, but acknowledged the municipality's efforts.

The Minister of Communications admitted that about 100,000 Starlink devices have entered Iran. He acknowledged that the government has failed to prevent people's access to social networks. He also said that the expansion of satellite internet will further reduce the Islamic Republic's control over the communication space.

Jamshid Barzegar said that in the absence of Mojtaba Khamenei, key decisions in the Islamic Republic have been handed over to a core group close to the Revolutionary Guards. He added that statements by Masoud Pezeshkian and Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf indicate increasing tensions among these factions. The continued absence of Mojtaba Khamenei has also increased ambiguity about the real decision-making authority in the Islamic Republic.

Amir Giti from Iran International said mutual distrust between the Islamic Republic, the IAEA, and Western countries has complicated inspectors' access to nuclear facilities. He added that Iran's concern about information leaking to the US and Israel is more of a leverage tactic in future negotiations. This issue stems from internal disagreements and mutual distrust.
Bank Melli has confirmed disruptions and discrepancies in some accounts. Transaction corrections and balance updates are ongoing. Customers complain about not having access to their account balances.

During a parliamentary energy commission meeting to investigate the causes of nationwide power outages, the electricity went out. This incident is seen as a bitter irony in the Islamic Republic. The topic was discussed by Kambiz Hosseini in a program.

The United States is reviewing the deployment of its forces in Europe and has asked European countries to take primary responsibility for their own defense. This move follows Trump's criticism of European countries for not doing more to assist the US in the war with the Islamic Republic. European diplomats are trying to assure the Pentagon that they are increasing their defense activities.

Anna Kelly, the principal deputy White House spokesperson, stated that there are no ongoing or planned negotiations with the Islamic Republic. Donald Trump also said there is no specific timeline for resuming talks and he is in no hurry. Trump added that both military attacks and economic pressure by the US against the Islamic Republic have been effective.

Bloomberg reported, citing officials, that a number of US allies believe the Strait of Hormuz has not yet been fully demined. These sources estimated the number of mines laid by the Islamic Republic at around 80 to 150, but the exact number of remaining mines is unknown. This assessment contradicts statements by Donald Trump about the waterway's clearance.

Scott Perry, a Republican member of the US House of Representatives, said the Islamic Republic should not be allowed to obtain nuclear weapons. He added that Donald Trump seeks to end the conflict quickly. These remarks follow the Trump administration's stance on Iran's nuclear program.

Meta has reached a settlement of up to $18 billion with 48 US states over allegations that Instagram and Facebook are addictive for children. This agreement halts several ongoing trials, and Meta is required to implement new protective measures for children and teenagers. However, thousands of individuals and hundreds of school districts still have complaints against Meta and other social media networks.

Nepalese officials initially attributed the deadly flood to an earthquake, but studies indicate a landslide of rock and ice blocked a river. The breaking of this natural dam caused a devastating wave of water and mud, killing at least 160 people and leaving hundreds missing. Experts have not yet confirmed a definite link between this disaster and climate change.

A Politico report shows bipartisan support in the US Congress for sanctioning Chinese banks that assist Iran's financial flow has increased. These sanctions could have broad consequences for the global financial system. Concerns about China's possible retaliatory response have also been raised.

Washington Stand, a conservative American media, analyzed threats by Barron Trump and an alleged attempt to kill one of Netanyahu's sons as reflecting the Islamic Republic's view of political leaders' families. It highlighted the role of family loyalty in the power structure of the Islamic Republic. The analysis also compared this with the influence of political families in the US.

The US Navy plans to deploy the aircraft carrier Theodore Roosevelt with five thousand crew members on a seven-month mission to the Middle East, which may extend to eight months. This carrier will replace the USS George Washington and will depart from San Diego. The average deployment duration of US aircraft carriers has increased to eight and a half months.

Miad Maleki stated that reviving maritime prize courts could allow the US Department of Justice to seize oil tankers and cargo related to the Islamic Republic. He added that this could severely impact shipping companies and the network circumventing sanctions. Seizing a few ships could result in the loss of hundreds of millions of dollars in assets.

Kayhan newspaper wrote that the steadfastness of the Iranian people and armed forces has caused the White House to return to the cycle of sanctions. Kayhan stated that Tehran is changing the rules of the game and will target US positions in the region. The newspaper warned that if sanctions continue, the US must bear the heavy costs of insecurity in the region.

Mehrdad Ghasemfar commented on Trump's statements about Mojtaba Khamenei's health, saying the main issue is his ability to lead the Islamic Republic. He added that if Mojtaba Khamenei cannot play the role of arbitrator for Ali Khamenei, the Islamic Republic will face a serious existential crisis.
